MacroTracker.title: Macro Liquidity Tracker
MacroTracker.description: Monitor when the 'market plumbing' is about to break. The Net Liquidity Index is the single most important number for 2026.

rrp.title: Reverse Repo (RRP) Balance
rrp.description: Total dollar amount in the Fed's Overnight Reverse Repo facility

bankReserves.title: Bank Reserves
bankReserves.description: Total reserve balances at Federal Reserve Banks

fedBalanceSheet.title: Fed Balance Sheet
fedBalanceSheet.description: Total assets of the Federal Reserve

tga.title: Treasury General Account (TGA)
tga.description: Treasury's operating account at the Fed

treasury10Y.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield
treasury10Y.description: Current yield to monitor the cost of borrowing

sofrIorbSpread.title: SOFR-IORB Spread
sofrIorbSpread.description: Difference between SOFR and Interest on Reserve Balances (in basis points)

highYieldSpreads.title: High-Yield Credit Spreads
highYieldSpreads.description: Spread between risky corporate debt and safe government bonds

vix.title: VIX (Volatility Index)
vix.description: Market volatility indicator (proxy for MOVE Index)

sofrSpread.threshold: Above 20 bps - banks desperate for cash

green.title: Green (Healthy)
green.description: Net Liquidity Index ≥ $3T. Market liquidity conditions are healthy. The financial system has sufficient reserves to handle normal operations and stress.

yellow.title: Yellow (Warning)
yellow.description: Net Liquidity Index between $2T and $3T. Market liquidity is becoming constrained. Monitor closely as conditions may deteriorate.

red.title: Red (Critical)
red.description: Net Liquidity Index < $2T. Market liquidity is critically low. The 'market plumbing' is at risk of breaking, which could lead to volatility, funding stress, or systemic issues.

netLiquidity.title: Net Liquidity Index
netLiquidity.description: The most important metric for 2026. Calculated as Fed Balance Sheet minus Treasury General Account minus Reverse Repo. This represents the actual liquidity available in the financial system. When this number drops too low, the market's ability to function smoothly is at risk.

rrp.title: Reverse Repo (RRP) Balance
rrp.description: Money market funds and other institutions parking excess cash with the Fed overnight. High RRP balances indicate excess liquidity in the system. When RRP drains, that liquidity moves into the broader market.

bankReserves.title: Bank Reserves
bankReserves.description: Cash that commercial banks hold at the Federal Reserve. These reserves are the foundation of the banking system's ability to lend and meet withdrawal demands. Declining reserves can signal tightening conditions.

fedBalanceSheet.title: Fed Balance Sheet
fedBalanceSheet.description: Total assets held by the Federal Reserve, primarily Treasury securities and mortgage-backed securities. The size of the balance sheet directly impacts system-wide liquidity. Quantitative tightening (QT) reduces this, tightening liquidity.

tga.title: Treasury General Account (TGA)
tga.description: The Treasury's checking account at the Fed. When the TGA increases, money is drained from the banking system. When it decreases (through spending), money flows back into the system, increasing liquidity.

treasury10Y.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield
treasury10Y.description: The interest rate on 10-year U.S. government bonds. This is a key indicator of borrowing costs and market expectations. Rising yields can indicate tightening financial conditions or inflation expectations.

sofrIorbSpread.title: SOFR-IORB Spread
sofrIorbSpread.description: The difference between the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) and the Interest on Reserve Balances (IORB). If SOFR spikes above IORB (spread > 20 bps), it means banks are desperate for cash and willing to pay more than the Fed's 'safe' rate to get it. This is a critical early warning signal that the 'market plumbing' is blocked.

highYieldSpreads.title: High-Yield Credit Spreads
highYieldSpreads.description: The gap between risky corporate debt and 'safe' government bonds. Widening spreads indicate that lenders are becoming afraid of defaults—a key sign that the 'bottom' of the K-shaped economy is failing. This often precedes broader market stress.

vix.title: VIX (Volatility Index)
vix.description: While the VIX tracks stock market volatility, it serves as a proxy for bond market volatility (MOVE Index). High VIX levels often precede equity crashes and indicate market stress. It measures the 'heartbeat' of market fear.
